transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I keep thinking my clients would be better off if I just weren’t here, and those thoughts about not wanting to wake up are starting to scare me. I've just been feeling really overwhelmed, and a colleague helped me set up this appointment because they were worried about me.
Have you experienced similar periods of feeling this low or overwhelmed in the past, perhaps months or years ago, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?
No, I've never felt like this before. This is the very first time I've ever felt this low and completely overwhelmed.
Did these feelings of being overwhelmed begin specifically following a recent stressful life event or significant change in your personal or professional life?

Yeah, it all started about a month or five weeks ago after a really stressful stretch at work. We had a cluster of very difficult cases, and then I had a tense disagreement with my supervising clinician about treatment plans. It left me feeling completely incompetent and like I'm totally out of my depth, and I've just been spiraling since then.
If that stressful period at work were to resolve or if you were removed from that situation, do you feel your mood would likely return to your normal baseline?
I'm really not sure. Everything feels so heavy and hopeless right now that it's hard to imagine ever feeling like myself again, even if things at work changed.
Besides feeling overwhelmed and hopeless about work, have you noticed other changes, such as significant shifts in your sleep, appetite, or your ability to concentrate on things outside of your job?

Yes, my sleep is awful; I lie awake for hours replaying work and wake up exhausted at 5 a.m., and I've barely been eating because I have no appetite and my clothes are getting loose. On top of that, my brain feels like mud. I lose my train of thought constantly and struggle to make even the simplest decisions.
Beyond your professional challenges, have you lost interest or pleasure in the hobbies, activities, or personal relationships that you previously enjoyed?

Yeah, definitely. I used to love playing guitar and hanging out with my friends after work, but lately it all just feels completely pointless. Now, I'd honestly rather just sit alone in the dark staring at nothing than pretend I'm enjoying anything.

Do you feel this loss of interest and sense of pointlessness primarily when you think about work, or does it feel like a constant, underlying state that affects every part of your life regardless of what you are doing?

It's definitely not just about work; it feels like a constant weight affecting every part of my life. I no longer enjoy things I used to look forward to, like playing guitar or hanging out with my friends. Most days, I'd honestly rather just sit in the dark staring at nothing than try to pretend I'm enjoying anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your perception of reality, such as hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or feeling like your thoughts are being controlled or broadcast to others?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I definitely haven't heard any voices, seen things that aren't there, or felt like my thoughts are being controlled or broadcast.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have become noticeably slowed down, or conversely, that you feel physically restless and unable to sit still?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes like that. I don't think my movements or speech have slowed down, and I haven't felt physically restless either.

Would you describe your current feeling of hopelessness and lack of interest as being so severe that you are unable to function in your daily routine, or are you still managing to carry out basic self-care and essential tasks?

Yes, it has completely disrupted my ability to function. I’ve started calling in sick or leaving work early because I feel too overwhelmed to run my groups, and my documentation is piling up and getting flagged by my supervisor. Outside of work, I'm ignoring texts from my friends and letting basic chores like dishes and laundry pile up for days because I just can’t deal with anything.
